links.outcome: Whether students detected when AI changed their diagnostic ranking for better or worse (automation bias)
links.effect: Accuracy improved in 65 students and worsened in 26 after AI use. Both groups rated AI as more influential than students whose accuracy did not change (P = .006 and P = .001).
links.quote: Students benefited most from AI when their baseline reasoning was weakest but could not reliably distinguish helpful from harmful AI influence, consistent with automation bias.

unlisted_practices: Introductory AI lecture combined with AI-integrated case practice and faculty-led debriefing in pre-clerkship medical education

screen.reason: Evaluates medical students' clinical reasoning accuracy and automation bias before and after access to an AI chatbot in a simulated case; it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or compare outcomes with versus without a training intervention.
